Summary: Quick console walkthrough focused on per-route usage analytics, cost decomposition, and anomaly flags. Customer is evaluating Redwood for a production pilot (patient-facing triage AI) with strict security and latency budgets. They want per-endpoint chargeback and a short pilot to validate economics.
Topics: console per-route dashboards; token-level chargeback; model routing & fallbacks; dedicated vs hosted; VPC/private deployment; SOC2/KMS; sandbox pilot logistics
Action items (brief): see metadata action_items field
Links shared: 1) deck: https://rwd.internal/sales/deck/marigold-2028 (shortlink) 2) cost-proj spreadsheet (preview attached)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): all right folks, thanks for joining. we are gonna run through the Console — focused on per route economics and how you'll slice cost back to product teams. just a quick intro, i'm jordan, ae. priya and samir from the product team are with me.
[00:18] Alyssa (Marigold): hey thanks — Alyssa here. excited. we have like five routes in prod that matter — triage, notes-summarize, intake-form, lab-interpret, and billing-assist. our primary ask is accurate chargeback per route and a way to catch cost spikes.
[00:32] Priya (Redwood): perfect. our Console exposes per-route dashboards — you can tag endpoints and we map token usage back to routes, model variants, and runtime kernels. i'll pull up the demo org now. bear with me, screen share coming.
[00:50] Diego (Marigold): quick Q — can we map to our internal service name? we use some weird prefixes, would that break the grouping?
[00:58] Priya (Redwood): nope, you can provide route tags at the SDK or via the proxy. we also support auto-discovery if you push the route header. sometimes the auto-discover mislabels, like in earlier builds it garbled k8s names, but we added a mask for that.
[01:15] [screen share sound, brief silence]
[01:35] Priya (Redwood): ok pulling up Route Overview. here's the heat map — X axis time, Y axis routes. you can see token counts, avg latency, and the estimated cost column. that estimate is driven by the model and the per-token unit cost profile — we surface both gross token charge and a normalized CPU/GPU cost split.
[02:03] Meera (Marigold): how accurate is that normalized split? finance will want something they can import into our chargeback engine.
[02:12] Samir (Redwood): good question. the Console produces CSV exports that include token tallies, model used, latency buckets, and a cost attribution line that matches the bill. for dedicated customers we can augment with actual GPU-hour billing to improve accuracy — the default is an inferred unit-cost model which is within ~5-12% for typical workloads. that's been our observed range.
[02:36] Tom (Marigold): security — where does data residency show up? we need to be able to say which requests never left eu-west-1.
[02:44] Priya (Redwood): region is a dimension in the dashboard. for Private customers we add a residency flag and a link to the audit log entry. also we keep request-level identifiers for up to your retention window (configurable).
[03:03] Alyssa (Marigold): you mentioned anomaly flags? can we get alerts if a single route spikes tokens unexpectedly?
[03:09] Priya (Redwood): yes — anomaly detection can be set per route or per project. thresholding is token-based or dollar-based; we also have adaptive baselining so it won't noise out on expected weekly cycles. you can push alerts to slack, pagerduty, or webhook.
[03:28] Diego (Marigold): any false positive issues? we had a vendor that alerted every small holiday surge and it was useless.
[03:34] Priya (Redwood): fair — we tune sensitivity and include learning windows. show you an example: see this stripe on the right, it marked a sudden change but then demoted because it matched a scheduled traffic replay.
[03:50] [keyboard clacks, brief crosstalk]
[04:06] Priya (Redwood): switching to Route Cost Breakdown for triage endpoint. top panel: tokens by prompt vs completion, middle: model family breakdown, bottom: per-minute cost attribution. note the colors represent model variants — gpt-like, redwood-xx, quantized variants.
[04:35] Alyssa (Marigold): our triage uses long contexts sometimes — like 4k tokens. how do you handle KV cache and prefix caching? because that changes per-token cost drastically.
[04:46] Samir (Redwood): we surface cache hits as a metric and show cost-savings from prefix/KV caching. Console includes a cache-utilization widget; if you turn on prefix caching the dashboard can project savings based on historical reuse patterns. in general, long contexts are where caching helps the most.
[05:05] Diego (Marigold): do you show model latency SLO breaches per route? we need to know if a cheaper model causes latency regressions.
[05:12] Priya (Redwood): yes, latency bands are charted per model route. you can overlay cost per token to see the latency vs cost tradeoff. we also support automated fallback policies — if a variant misses SLO it will route to a faster model.
[05:29] Alyssa (Marigold): we prefer to keep deterministic responses for clinical pathways — can't have silent model switching unless it's auditable.
[05:37] Jordan (Redwood): totally — all rollouts and automatic fallbacks are logged and you can enforce manual approval or require canary windows. we also provide structured audit trails for every decision.
[05:52] Meera (Marigold): on the finance side, can we tag usage by cost center and generate a monthly alloc table?
[05:58] Samir (Redwood): yep — you can tag routes with cost center metadata and export a monthly allocation spreadsheet. there's also a chargeback API if you want to pull nightly summaries into your internal billing system.
[06:14] Diego (Marigold): network / private deploy question — if we do Private (VPC), how do you collect telemetry? we can't have outbound telemetry to third-party.
[06:22] Priya (Redwood): for Private deployments the telemetry agent runs inside your VPC and writes to a customer-managed telemetry store. we provide the console UI via a control-plane connection; for air-gapped setups we can provide a local console so no outbound egress is required.
[06:38] Tom (Marigold): KMS — we have an internal HSM. any support for envelope encryption?
[06:43] Samir (Redwood): yes, we support KMS integrations and envelope encryption patterns. we'll share the integration doc.
[06:50] [brief pause, screen scroll noise]
[07:05] Priya (Redwood): switching to the Cost Explorer. you can slice by route, model, user, and label. here i filter to last 30 days and group by model variant. notice how the quantized route shows lower per-token cost but slightly higher latency — the console surfaces both so you can choose.
[07:32] Alyssa (Marigold): interesting, can you show a predicted 30-day spend if we change routing policy to prefer quantized for non-critical routes?
[07:39] Jordan (Redwood): yep — there's a what-if simulator. i'll set a policy: prefer quantized for 60% of low-priority traffic and keep gold model for 40%. simulator runs and shows an estimated 34% cost reduction and a 12% latency increase on the quantized portion.
[08:00] Meera (Marigold): that's the sort of number we need for stakeholder buy-in. can you run that against our historical traffic?
[08:07] Priya (Redwood): if you grant access to a replay or give a small dataset we can run a pilot replay in the sandbox and produce an empirical projection. that's what we usually do for pilots.
[08:21] Alyssa (Marigold): pilot length? we were thinking 2 weeks but maybe 48h is enough to validate economics?
[08:28] Jordan (Redwood): for cost validation 48-72 hours of realistic traffic replay is usually sufficient. for quality regressions you might want longer. propose: 48h pilot to start.
[08:39] Diego (Marigold): onboarding effort — what does our infra team need to do?
[08:43] Priya (Redwood): minimal. integrate the SDK or proxy (we have a lightweight sidecar) and tag routes. if you're using Private, there's some VPC setup and firewall rules. we'll provide a runbook.
[08:55] [crosstalk: "runbook" / "ip ranges"]
[09:10] Priya (Redwood): now show the Alerts & Budget panel. you can set hard budget caps per team which trigger throttling or soft alerts. many finops teams like to auto-tag then notify budget owners.
[09:28] Meera (Marigold): do you support per-token chargeback to downstream teams? we need to bill internal product groups monthly.
[09:34] Samir (Redwood): yes — the export contains pre-aggregated chargeback lines per cost center. we can also push to your accounting SFTP endpoint nightly if you want automated ingestion.
[09:48] Alyssa (Marigold): are historical audit logs easily queryable? our compliance folks will ask for request traces for specific patient interactions.
[09:56] Tom (Marigold): yeah that's critical. retention windows and PII handling matter.
[10:02] Priya (Redwood): logs are queryable; for PII-sensitive flows we recommend tokenizing identifiers at the edge and storing only linkage keys. audit logs include metadata and model input/output hashes but you can opt into or out of storing raw text. we'll share the privacy playbook.
[10:22] Diego (Marigold): what about cost smoothing? some months we spike because of research experiments and we prefer to amortize that over the quarter for finance.
[10:30] Jordan (Redwood): we don't do amortization in-console automatically, but you can export and apply smoothing in your internal pipeline. we can help set up a recommended export format.
[10:40] [brief pause]
[11:00] Priya (Redwood): quick detour — here's the Route Insights view which surfaces top contributors to cost. it uses SHAP-like attribution to show token groups and prompt templates that drive spend. often you find a few prompts responsible for 60% of tokens.
[11:22] Alyssa (Marigold): that would be gold. we had one prompt that leaked a bunch of context because of a broken loop in the front end.
[11:29] Priya (Redwood): the insights view also surfaces suggested optimizations — e.g., shorter templates, turn on prefix caching, or switch to a smaller model for certain intents. it's opinionated but exportable.
[11:45] Meera (Marigold): regarding pricing, is there special pricing for healthcare clients? any compliance premiums?
[11:52] Jordan (Redwood): pricing is usage-based; for healthcare we do enterprise terms that bundle SOC2/compliance support and longer retention. i'll include a compliance addendum option in the quote.
[12:04] Diego (Marigold): competitor question — why pick Redwood vs Anthropic's hosted offering?
[12:10] Samir (Redwood): short answer: strong runtime optimizations + unified tooling across hosted/dedicated/private. we give you predictable economics controls (batching, cache, quantization) and the same Console whether you're on our hosted cloud or Private in your VPC. many competitors focus just on model access not the operational cost levers.
[12:31] Alyssa (Marigold): also important — can we lock model versions per route for auditability?
[12:37] Priya (Redwood): yes — pinning model versions is supported and shows up in the rollout history. you can lock to a commit hash or a verified release.
[12:47] [screen flicker, brief pause]
[13:05] Priya (Redwood): demo: create a canary rule — route triage, 10% gold model, 90% quantized, monitor latency band and error rate. i'll create it now.
[13:21] [typing sounds]
[13:45] Priya (Redwood): okay canary created — timeline view shows real-time split and the ability to abort and roll back. logs are attached per request so you can replay failing cases locally.
[14:02] Meera (Marigold): love that. who gets notified on auto-fallback? can we send it to a product owner and not the whole eng channel?
[14:09] Priya (Redwood): yes — notification routing is configurable by alert rule. you can scope recipients to Slack channels, emails, or a webhook which can then fan out internally.
[14:24] Alyssa (Marigold): any gotchas with long context triage + quantization? i'm worried quality will drop.
[14:31] Samir (Redwood): quantization helps cost but can affect long-context behavior. for triage we recommend hybrid: keep gold for initial context parsing, quantize for follow-ups, and use KV caching. pilot will surface quality delta.
[14:48] Diego (Marigold): technnical deep dive later — we might want an SE session to benchmark our flows.
[14:55] Jordan (Redwood): sure — we can schedule a 90m performance check where we run a replay and measure p50/p95 p99.
[15:03] Tom (Marigold): security checklist — SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit trail, encryption, retention window, and penetration testing. do you support SCIM?
[15:12] Priya (Redwood): yes we support SAML and SCIM for provisioning, RBAC with fine-grained roles, and we publish a penetration testing policy. we'll drop the security package into your inbox after the call.
[15:28] Alyssa (Marigold): about pricing — do you charge per token and then a separate hosting fee for Dedicated?
[15:34] Jordan (Redwood): hosted is straightforward per-token plus minor monthly service fee for support tiers. Dedicated includes reserved capacity and a base platform fee; we can model the per-token economics for each. i'll include both scenarios in the quote.
[15:49] Meera (Marigold): can you show the Billing Export format quickly?
[15:55] Priya (Redwood): sure — here's a sample CSV: timestamp, route, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, region, cost_usd, cost_center. you can drop it into your accounting pipeline.
[16:08] Alyssa (Marigold): perfect. any limits on export retention?
[16:12] Samir (Redwood): exports are available as long as your retention window. for hosted customers we default to 90 days; enterprise can set longer retention or request log snapshots.
[16:25] Diego (Marigold): one small thing — our observability stack is Splunk. can you push logs there?
[16:30] Priya (Redwood): yep, we have a Splunk forwarder and generic webhook sinks.
[16:37] [pause]
[16:50] Priya (Redwood): demo closing — show the Optimize suggestions engine. it looks at your routes and suggests batching configs, cache TTLs, and where quantization would most help. it's advisory and includes projected savings.
[17:10] Meera (Marigold): the optimizer sounds like it ties into your earlier "what-if" sim — nice. who reviews those suggestions? is it automated?
[17:16] Samir (Redwood): suggestions are auto-generated but require manual opt-in to apply. you can schedule periodic reviews or export the suggestions to a Google Sheet for your FinOps team to triage.
[17:31] Alyssa (Marigold): final questions from my side — what's the typical pilot timeline and success criteria?
[17:37] Jordan (Redwood): pilot: 48h traffic replay + 1 week for validation and report. success criteria: within 10% of projected cost savings, no regression in the clinical intent accuracy (Alyssa's team decides), and integration with your chargeback pipeline.
[17:53] Alyssa (Marigold): sounds reasonable.
[18:01] Diego (Marigold): ops question — how much instrumentation change is required for the SDK switch?
[18:06] Priya (Redwood): minimal — most customers swap in the SDK and set route tags, then flip traffic via feature flags. we provide a sidecar if you prefer a non-intrusive path.
[18:20] Tom (Marigold): security will expect the SOC2 docs and an architectural diagram showing where logs go.
[18:27] Jordan (Redwood): we'll send the SOC2 pack and a sample network diagram — action item noted.
[18:34] [several brief confirmations]
[18:50] Samir (Redwood): quick recap — we showed per-route dashboards, cost breakdown, anomaly flags, what-if sims, optimizer suggestions, and rollout controls.
[19:03] Jordan (Redwood): next steps: i'll send pricing and pilot docs, priya will spin up the sandbox, samir will share the routing playbook and quantization notes, and tom will get the security pack.
[19:17] Alyssa (Marigold): thanks everyone — we'll follow up after our internal review.
[19:25] Jordan (Redwood): great — we'll email the assets and aim to start the pilot early next week. thanks for your time.
[19:34] [end recording noise]
